limitations: Deletions and unwanted changes can propagate to other devices; synchronization alone is not an independent backup.
Peers need connectivity and time online to exchange changes; desktop tray applications are separate projects from the core daemon.
File versioning is disabled by default and cannot archive an earlier version when the file is changed locally on the same device.

features: File versioning can archive older files received from other devices; it is configured per folder and per device.

limitations: Cloud storage limits and provider charges remain separate from the backup client.
Backup encryption credentials and a tested restore procedure are essential; optional management features have separate free and paid plans.
Portable mode documents server-data placement, not proof that every cache, temporary file, credential or OS artifact stays in one folder; relocation and restore still need testing.

features: The documented --portable-mode places its data folder in a data directory beside the program files; --server-datafolder or DUPLICATI_HOME can explicitly select the server data location.

limitations: Sync operations can delete destination files to match the source; review the direction and use the documented dry-run option for unfamiliar jobs.
Provider API limits, credentials, storage charges and filesystem differences still apply; this is primarily a command-line workflow.
For a transfer that must retain destination-only files, use copy rather than sync; preview sync with --dry-run or --interactive because sync may delete destination files.
